# Bad Tape: MIDI implementation

Every parameter of the pedal can be set over the Seed's USB MIDI port: Control Change for the parameters with a CC (the factory knob functions, the switches and FS1), 14-bit NRPN and SysEx for all 131 of them. The parameter table `daisy/src/params.h` is the single source of truth; this file is generated from it.

## Channels

The pedal receives on all channels (omni) and never sends CC or NRPN: a MIDI change is applied silently (the log line `midi NAME = VALUE UNIT` reports the stored value). Changes made on the pedal's controls are not sent as MIDI either; with WATCH on, the SysEx link streams every change, MIDI included, as VALUE.

## Control Change

A CC value 0-127 maps to 0..1 along the parameter's taper (`value/127`, see Tapers). For an on/off parameter 0-63 is off and 64-127 is on.

|CC|Parameter|Control|
|---|---|---|
|14|`delay_mix`||
|15|`reverb_mix`||
|16|`hall_space`||
|17|`delay_time`||
|18|`delay_feedback`||
|19|`delay_color`||
|20|`plate_space`||
|21|`canyon_space`||
|22|`delay_mode`|SW1|
|23|`delay_type`|SW2|
|24|`reverb_algo`|SW3|
|25|`bypass`|FS1|

## NRPN

- Select a parameter with CC 99 (NRPN MSB) = id >> 7 and CC 98 (NRPN LSB) = id & 0x7F; numbers >= 131 are ignored.
- CC 6 (data entry MSB) sets the parameter to code `msb << 7` at once; a following CC 38 (data entry LSB) refines it to `msb << 7 | lsb`. A CC 38 alone uses the last data MSB since the selection (0 if none).
- The code (0-16383) maps to 0..1 as `code/16383` along the parameter's taper. Code 0 is exactly the minimum, 16383 exactly the maximum.
- Data entry is ignored until both CC 99 and CC 98 have been received on that channel. CC 101/100 (RPN select) and the null NRPN (99 = 127, 98 = 127) deselect; CC 96/97 (increment/decrement) are ignored. Each channel keeps its own selection.

## Tapers

With `n` in 0..1 (CC `value/127`, NRPN/SysEx `code/16383`):

- linear: `value = min + n * (max - min)`
- log: `value = min * (max/min)^n`
- audio: `value = min + (max - min) * (32^n - 1)/31`, like an A-taper pot: 15 % of the range at n = 0.5
- enum: `value = min + round(n * (max - min))`; the canonical code of an enum value is `round((value - min)/(max - min) * 16383)`

## SysEx

Frames are `F0 7D 62 02 <cmd> <payload> F7` (manufacturer 7D, device 62, version 02; `daisy/src/link.h`). Ids, counts and codes travel as two 7-bit bytes `hi = v >> 7`, `lo = v & 0x7F`. Version-01 frames (the previous one-byte-id format) are ignored, except that `daisy/tools/usb_log.py --dfu` sends DFU in both versions. `daisy/tools/usb_log.py` implements the host side (`--dump`, `--get`, `--set`, `--check-params`).

|Direction|Command|Payload|Effect|
|---|---|---|---|
|host to pedal|`02` GET|`<id hi> <id lo>`|answered by VALUE|
|host to pedal|`03` SET|`<id hi> <id lo> <hi> <lo>`|sets the parameter (as a MIDI write, see Arbitration); answered by VALUE with the stored code (an enum's canonical code)|
|host to pedal|`04` DUMP|none|answered by one PARAM per id, then DUMP END; a DUMP during a dump restarts it|
|host to pedal|`05` WATCH|`<on>` (0 or 1)|on: the pedal streams VALUE for every parameter whose code changed for any reason (knob, switch, FS1, link, MIDI), checked every 20 ms; knob jitter of a few codes is absorbed. Off is the boot default|
|host to pedal|`07` SAVE|`<id hi> <id lo> ...`|saves each parameter's current value as its power-up value, in one flash write; answered by SAVED per id (only on success), then STORE|
|host to pedal|`08` CLEAR|`<id hi> <id lo> ...`|forgets the saved values (power-up uses the default); same replies as SAVE; with nothing to change there is no flash write and the status is 0|
|host to pedal|`09` SAVED?|none|answered by SAVED for every saveable id in id order, then SAVED END|
|pedal to host|`13` VALUE|`<id hi> <id lo> <hi> <lo>`|the parameter's current code|
|pedal to host|`14` PARAM|`<id hi> <id lo> <taper> <control> <cc> <group> <def hi> <def lo> <cur hi> <cur lo> <text>`|one table entry; text is ASCII `name\|unit\|min\|max` (min/max as `%g`)|
|pedal to host|`15` DUMP END|`<count hi> <count lo>`|the dump is complete; count = 131|
|pedal to host|`16` SAVED|`<id hi> <id lo> <has> <hi> <lo>`|has 1: the code of the saved value; has 0: the code of the default|
|pedal to host|`17` STORE|`<status>`|0 ok, 1 the flash write failed (nothing changed), 2 bad request (no write)|
|pedal to host|`18` SAVED END|`<count hi> <count lo>`|the SAVED? answer is complete; count = 127 saveable parameters|

Saved values: SAVE persists a parameter's current value to flash (QSPI 0x903FE000, two 4 KB slots) as its power-up value; parameters on a switch or FS1 are not saveable. A SAVE/CLEAR with no id, an odd payload, an id >= 131 or a parameter on a switch or FS1 logs `link: bad save message CC` and answers STORE 2. A WATCH with a wrong length or on > 1 logs `link: bad watch message`.

A GET/SET with an id >= 131 or a wrong length, or a DUMP with a payload, logs `link: bad param message CC` and gets no reply. Enum bytes in PARAM: taper 0 linear, 1 log, 2 enum, 3 audio; control 0 none, 1-3 SW1-SW3, 4 FS1; group 0 global, 1 delay, 2 hall, 3 plate, 4 canyon, 5 eq, 6 knobs.

## Arbitration

What you see is what you get, with exceptions for MIDI, FS2 and remapping:

- Knob slots: `knob_N_primary` and `knob_N_secondary` (parameter ids, 255 = none) choose what knob N drives without FS2 and with FS2 held. Factory primaries: knob 1 `delay_mix`, knob 2 `reverb_mix`, knob 3 `hall_space`, knob 4 `delay_time`, knob 5 `delay_feedback`, knob 6 `delay_color`; the factory secondaries are none. Switch and FS1 parameters and the assignments themselves cannot be assigned (they mean none). Any `*_space` id means the active algorithm's Space macro.
- Primaries are what you see is what you get. A MIDI or SysEx write to a parameter on a slot holds it until that slot's knob moves more than 3 % of its travel from where it was at the write; then the knob takes the parameter back (the log shows `knob N takes NAME`, or `knob N fs2 takes NAME` for a secondary).
- FS2: pressed after 5 ms of steady contact, released after 30 ms. While it is held a knob drives only its secondary, once the knob has moved more than 3 % from where it was at the press. A knob moved more than 3 % while FS2 was held keeps its primary until it moves more than 3 % from where it was at the release.
- A parameter on more than one slot follows the knob that moved last.
- A newly assigned parameter keeps its value until its knob moves more than 3 %.
- A switch that changes position always sets its parameter; a switch that has not moved leaves a MIDI value alone. FS1 toggles bypass.
- A Space slot drives the active reverb algorithm's macro (SW3 / `reverb_algo`): `plate_space` (plate), `hall_space` (hall) or `canyon_space` (canyon). The others keep their last value. A held Space parameter stays held when its algorithm becomes active, until its knob moves more than 3 %.
- Parameters on no slot keep whatever MIDI last set (default or saved value at power-on).
- Saved values apply at power-up; the knob replaces the saved value of a parameter on a primary slot. A saved link target is held like a MIDI write, anchored at its source's first change after power-up, until the source moves more than 3 % from there.
- Links: when a source parameter changes (from its knob or MIDI) it writes its targets, except targets on a knob slot (the knob owns them). A MIDI write to a target holds it until the source moves more than 3 % of its travel from where it was at the write. Each Space macro runs 0-100 % (n = value/100) from a small, short space to a large, long one, and its default gives its targets' defaults: `hall_space` writes `hall_rt_mid` = 0.4 * 25^n s; `hall_space` writes `hall_size` = 39 - 36 (1 - n)^2 m; `hall_space` writes `hall_shape` = 35 + 30 n %; `hall_space` writes `hall_spread` = 20 + 60 n %; `plate_space` writes `plate_size` = 180 n - 80 n^2 %; `plate_space` writes `plate_mid_decay` = 0.36 * 25^n s; `plate_space` writes `plate_lf_decay` = 0.36 * 25^n s; `plate_space` writes `plate_depth` = 20 + 60 n %; `canyon_space` writes `canyon_master_delay` = 30 + 110 n - 40 n^2 %; `canyon_space` writes `canyon_feedback` = 100 - 40 (1 - n)^3 %; `canyon_space` writes `canyon_master_depth` = 20 + 60 n %.
